mesh_2_1.material: Fiberglass Composite (GFRP) or Carbon Fiber Reinforced Polymer (CFRP)
mesh_2_1.description: Reduces aerodynamic drag while protecting the payload and recovery system during flight.
mesh_2_1.fullDescription: The nose cone is the foremost aerodynamic component of a rocket. Its streamlined profile minimizes pressure drag and helps maintain stable airflow throughout ascent. It protects internal payloads and transfers aerodynamic loads into the main airframe.

specifications.Design Objective: Minimum drag with adequate structural strength

mesh_2_1.engineeringNotes: The nose cone profile is selected to minimize drag while maintaining structural integrity. Composite construction provides high stiffness with low mass and is widely used in sounding rockets and high-power rockets.

Payload-1.description: Houses payloads, avionics, sensors, telemetry equipment and recovery electronics.
Payload-1.fullDescription: The payload bay provides a protected compartment for scientific instruments, electronics, cameras, or experimental payloads. It is designed for easy integration while maintaining structural integrity during launch and recovery.
Payload-1.engineeringNotes: Payload bays are commonly designed with removable couplers or access panels to simplify installation and maintenance of avionics and scientific payloads.

Bulkhead-1.description: Separates rocket compartments while transferring structural loads.
Bulkhead-1.fullDescription: Bulkheads are structural members that connect adjacent rocket sections. They transfer axial, bending, and shear loads while providing mounting locations for recovery systems, payloads, and couplers.

specifications.Integration: Compatible with couplers and recovery hardware

Bulkhead-1.engineeringNotes: Bulkheads are typically machined with weight reduction features while maintaining adequate stiffness for flight loads.

Main_Body_Tube-1.material: Carbon Fiber Composite, Fiberglass Composite or Phenolic Tube
Main_Body_Tube-1.description: Primary structural member supporting the complete launch vehicle.
Main_Body_Tube-1.fullDescription: The body tube forms the main airframe of the rocket. It connects all structural components and carries thrust, aerodynamic, bending, and landing loads throughout the mission.
Main_Body_Tube-1.engineeringNotes: Body tubes are designed to resist buckling while minimizing structural weight. Composite airframes are preferred for their excellent stiffness-to-weight ratio.

Fins-1.material: G10 Fiberglass, Carbon Fiber Composite or Aircraft Grade Plywood
Fins-1.description: Provides aerodynamic stability by keeping the rocket aligned with the flight path.
Fins-1.fullDescription: Rocket fins generate restoring aerodynamic forces whenever the vehicle deviates from its intended trajectory. Proper fin sizing ensures static stability while minimizing aerodynamic drag.
Fins-1.engineeringNotes: Fin geometry is selected to achieve adequate stability margin while minimizing structural weight and aerodynamic drag.

Tail_Section-1.material: Aluminium Alloy, Phenolic Composite and Steel Hardware
Tail_Section-1.description: Houses the propulsion system and transfers thrust into the airframe.
Tail_Section-1.fullDescription: The motor section integrates the propulsion system, motor mount, retention hardware, and thermal protection components. It safely transfers thrust loads into the rocket structure during powered flight.
Tail_Section-1.engineeringNotes: Motor mounts are designed for rapid replacement while ensuring reliable load transfer and thermal protection during motor operation.

mesh_2.material: Fiberglass Composite, Carbon Fiber Composite or Phenolic Tube
mesh_2.description: Connects the nose cone to the airframe while maintaining structural alignment.
mesh_2.fullDescription: The shoulder or coupler fits inside the body tube and provides a secure mechanical interface between rocket sections. It maintains alignment while allowing easy separation for payload access or recovery deployment.
mesh_2.engineeringNotes: Couplers are designed with tight manufacturing tolerances to ensure reliable alignment while preventing excessive friction during separation events.
